children: AceVector files RHP for Snapdeal IPO, cutting fresh issue to Rs 287 crore and OFS by 34.9 per cent ahead of the September 25 opening

Snapdeal parent AceVector Ltd has filed its red herring prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, nearly a year after receiving observations from the market regulator on its confidential IPO filing, as per a media report.
The company raised Rs 13 crore in a pre-IPO placement, reducing the fresh issue size to Rs 287 crore from the Rs 300 crore proposed in its updated draft red herring prospectus filed in December 2025.
The offer-for-sale component has also been reduced by 34.9 per cent to 4.16 crore shares from 6.39 crore shares proposed earlier.

SoftBank's selling entity Starfish I Pte Ltd has reduced its offer-for-sale portion by 34.8 per cent to 2.76 crore shares from 4.23 crore shares. Starfish I is part of AceVector's promoter group and holds a 30.68 per cent stake in the company.

Three Nexus-affiliated entities, Nexus India Direct Investments II, Nexus Opportunity Fund Ltd and Nexus Ventures III Ltd, will collectively sell 86.96 lakh shares, down from 1.33 crore shares proposed earlier. Foxconn-backed FIH Business Global plans to sell 17.41 lakh shares.
Individual investor Priyanka Shreevar Kheruka, who had proposed to sell 19.37 lakh shares in the earlier filing, will not participate in the offer for sale.
Other selling shareholders include Jason Ashok Kothari, Rupen Investment and Industries and Centaurus Trading and Investments.
AceVector's IPO will open for public subscription on September 25, following anchor bidding on September 24, and will close on September 29.

AceVector is the parent company of value-commerce marketplace Snapdeal, house of brands platform Stellaro Brands and e-commerce SaaS company Unicommerce. The three businesses were consolidated under AceVector in 2022.
The company first filed its IPO documents through the confidential route in July 2025 and received regulatory approval in November.
IPO Proceeds
AceVector plans to use Rs 132 crore of the fresh issue proceeds for marketing and business promotion for Snapdeal between FY27 and FY29.

Of this, Rs 40 crore is earmarked for FY27, Rs 55 crore for FY28 and Rs 37 crore for FY29. The spending will cover digital and social media campaigns, influencer-led promotions, product discovery and performance marketing, with a focus on value-conscious consumers in Tier 2 and smaller cities.
The company also plans to invest Rs 50 crore in Snapdeal's technology infrastructure, including cloud computing, storage, networking and software.

AceVector said the technology investment will support AI-driven personalisation, customer engagement and retention, user experience improvements and A/B testing. The infrastructure is also used for order verification, fulfilment, logistics and demand forecasting.

Snapdeal incurred Rs 11.32 crore in hosting charges and Rs 7.83 crore in software expenses for its marketplace business in FY26. Its cloud infrastructure handled 13.79 million instance-hours, 32.57 petabytes-month of storage usage and 9.83 petabytes of network traffic during the fiscal year.
More than Rs 100 crore of the IPO proceeds will be allocated towards acquisitions. The company has not identified specific acquisition targets.
Financial Performance
AceVector's net loss narrowed nearly 64 per cent to Rs 45.5 crore in FY26 from Rs 126.3 crore in FY25.

The company had incurred Rs 73.6 crore in exceptional expenses in FY25, including Rs 57.9 crore towards an expected credit loss on a security deposit and Rs 15.7 crore in legal and professional expenses. No such exceptional expenses were recognised in FY26.
AceVector's operating revenue increased 29.1 per cent to Rs 510.4 crore in FY26 from Rs 395 crore in FY25.

Freight and collection income contributed Rs 257.9 crore to revenue, while its SaaS business generated Rs 204 crore. Revenue from marketing fees declined 16 per cent to Rs 25.7 crore, while sales of goods contributed around Rs 12.7 crore.
Including other income of Rs 27.3 crore, AceVector's total income stood at Rs 537.7 crore in FY26.
Total expenses increased 26.8 per cent to Rs 575.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 453.8 crore in the previous fiscal.
